page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.2xlarge is a burstable virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs and 8 physical cores mapped to an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

The CPU architecture is x86_64, supporting instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES cryptography, and FMA. Because the CPU allocation is burstable, the instance is designed to handle baseline workloads with the ability to burst to higher performance levels when CPU credits are available. Consequently, single-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, register in the bottom 10% of performance. Multi-core performance, however, reaches average tiers in stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests, though Geekbench multi-core and Passmark database operations fall into the weak category.

Memory performance is moderate, with cached and uncached read-only memory bandwidth tests scoring in the middle 50%. This profile translates to average throughput for Redis SET operations, while static web serving and small-model LLM inference tasks show weaker performance characteristics. The instance represents a budget-friendly tier, trading off sustained high-performance compute and local storage for cost efficiency in workloads with variable or low baseline CPU utilization. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, development environments, code compilation, and low-traffic database applications.
